title: Sitting in with Basie on brushes before Jo Jones
summary: Basie, unhappy with his drummer, asks Leeman to sit in; he plays brushes while out of work with the stranded Murphy band.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, he and Lips were my friends, and when I'd go up -- and Basie eventually asked me to sit in, I was scared to death, but I played a little. He wasn't too happy with his drummer. I'll give you his name later on, I can't think of it now. It's not Jo Jones, though.
This drummer you were speaking of -- you say it wasn't Jo Jones.
He didn't get the style of the band.
Uh huh. We can't recall his name.

And Basie, some night there, he would start, and he'd ask me "Do you want to play?" because I had played brushes one night, I didn't even pick up a stick. So I played brushes with him and he thought it was swing enough, he was very happy. That I could keep some time with him.
Well, this was when I was learning now. And we all became friends.
So you played with Basie for awhile then, in '34?
Well, when Jo came with the band -- see, Jo came in the band five or six months later, I came back, and I walked in one night and Basie was building the band.

We're not talking about when Jo came in -- we're talking about this drummer, whose name we can't recall -- you set in at first. Did you ever work with him regularly, with Basie -- did you come in and play regular?
Afterwards. I'll get to that. I have to tell you about Jo Jones, after Jo Jones came in.
But if it's going to be chronological,
we have to go from the time that this other guy whose name we can't recall --
I don't remember his name, no.
Well, who were you working with?
I was with Dan Murphy, and we were on a panic, as they used to call it. We were out of work for two days.
Just sat in with the band.
